runs.verdict: 191/7 on both legs. The probe ANSWERED and the pre-registered prediction holds exactly.

probe.t24.9: PASS -- Nix REFUSES an unsigned object into a LOCAL store with require-sigs=true. Signature checking is live in this environment.
probe.t24.10: PASS -- the SAME object, SAME config, into a BINARY CACHE destination is ACCEPTED.
probe.conclusion: Signature verification lives in the local store's add path. A file:// binary cache accepts anything. The only difference between the two probes is the destination type, and it decides the outcome.

establishedDefect.what: nse_tier_materialise copied the tier straight into the replica, which is a file:// binary cache. The SIGNATURE_UNTRUSTED branch was therefore UNREACHABLE -- not mis-worded or mis-classified, but a policy stated in an error message about a code path no input could reach.
establishedDefect.evidence: t24.11-t24.14 and t24.17/t24.18 red on a fixture whose preconditions (t24.1, t24.4, t24.5, t24.6, t24.7, t24.8) are all green, plus the t24.9/t24.10 pair that attributes the cause.
establishedDefect.alsoDemoted: t24.20-t24.23 (leg C) currently pass TRIVIALLY, because everything passes. Leg C is an attributable positive control only once legs A and B can fail. Until the fix lands, no part of t24 supports the policy claim.

fixtureNowSound: t24.7 the signed tier carries signatures
t24.8 BY the key this test generated -- the local-store signing route works where secret-key-files on a cache-to-cache copy did not
runs.fix: Materialise the tier through a LOCAL store, then push the verified objects to the replica with --no-check-sigs. Chosen because t24.9 MEASURED that a local destination enforces. `nix store verify --sigs` is cheaper but its flags across both Nix versions are unmeasured here, so it is gap-26 rather than an assumption. DESIGN.md 21d.

runs.kind: t24 third attempt -- first execution end to end
runs.verdict: 186/8 on both legs. flake check GREEN. The fixture preconditions hold, so for the first time the reds are FINDINGS rather than harness faults.

findings.assertion: t24.4 the signed tier really carries signatures -- expected something other than 0
findings.what: secret-key-files does NOT sign on a cache-to-cache nix copy; the signed tier had zero Sig: lines.
findings.why it matters: The same precondition PASSED in run 30 -- on cache.nixos.org signatures propagated from the host store. The signing mechanism had never once worked, in either run, and only a fixture with nothing to inherit could reveal it.
findings.correction: Signing now goes through a local store (copy in, nix store sign --store, copy out), and t24.8 requires the signatures to be BY THE GENERATED KEY, not merely present.

findings.assertion: t24.11 an unsigned tier object is refused, not accepted; t24.16 no manifest is written
findings.what: On a tier verified unsigned (t24.1, t24.5, t24.6 all green), preserve materialised the object and wrote a manifest. The SIGNATURE_UNTRUSTED branch did not fire.
findings.mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not guessed. 'This tool does not check' and 'Nix does not verify into a binary-cache destination' produce the same green leg.
findings.measuredNext: t24.9 requires Nix to REFUSE the same object into a local store (control that checking is live at all); t24.10 carries the pre-registered PREDICTION that a binary-cache destination accepts it. preserve.sh is unchanged until they answer. gap-25.

runs.verdict: RED on both legs. flake check failed on two shellcheck INFO findings, and the acceptance suite died after printing the t24 header with ZERO t24 assertions run.

cause.acceptance: stray=$(grep -l '^Sig: ' "$STRIP"/*.narinfo 2>/dev/null | wc -l). grep exits 1 on no match, pipefail propagates it, and a VARIABLE ASSIGNMENT takes its substitution's status, so set -e ended the run. The line asserted the stripped cache had NO signatures left, so the success case was the fatal one. Same shape as the find|head that killed run 7.
cause.flakeCheck: SC2012 (ls to count files) in tests/run-tests.sh and SC2016 in tests/unit-shell.sh. A local shellcheck run WITHOUT the flake's flags (-x -e SC1091 --shell=bash) exited non-zero on unrelated SC1091 notices and was reported as inconclusive rather than as a finding.

whatIsEstablished.aboutTheSignaturePolicy: NOTHING, for the second consecutive run. Run 30 measured a fixture that carried a trusted signature; run 31 never reached an assertion.

corrections: count_narinfos(): a loop with no pipe at all replaces every grep|wc in the t24 fixture.
u25 flags assignments (never arguments) that read from an unguarded grep; u25.2 drives it red on the exact line that killed this run.
One further live instance found and fixed: u20.9's rendered=$(grep -oE ... | tr | sort).
u26 runs the flake's exact shellcheck invocation locally, with u26.2 as its positive control. It turned red on the code written alongside it.

preRegistrationClassification.ruleAsWritten: leg A or B green -> the tier copy is not checking signatures at all; the POLICY is failing and the fix is in lib/preserve.sh, never in t24.
preRegistrationClassification.whyNot: t24.4 went red in the same run: the 'unsigned' tier carried 6 Sig: lines. The fixture copied the victim out of the HOST store, where objects substituted from cache.nixos.org keep that cache's signature in the store database, and nix copy propagates it. The tier was therefore signed by a key trusted BY DEFAULT, so leg A and leg B were accepted for a reason unconnected to the policy and leg C succeeded for a reason unconnected to the key.
preRegistrationClassification.correctClassification: FIXTURE DEFECT -- the section 21 case 't24.3 or t24.4 RED -> that is a fixture problem too'. The classification as written assumed the fixture was what it claimed.

status.nextRunPolicy: A further cold run of the same commit yields almost no information. The next run should exist because a new falsifiable claim exists.
status.resultStatement: Within the tested envelope, E1-E3 are confirmed, the claimed necessity of the workarounds is falsified, and removal of those workarounds preserves every pre-registered observable. The experiment protocol itself was prospectively validated, by rejecting a defective measurement criterion BEFORE the intervention.

note: The commit that closed the experimental line. Recorded by a later commit, because a commit cannot name its own hash -- the same measured/recorded split this file exists to keep straight.

status.runIndexPolicy: Only executions that carry an empirical claim are indexed as runs. A documentation commit still triggers CI; that execution is operational verification, not a new experiment, and is deliberately absent from `runs`. Otherwise the index becomes a graveyard of identical green executions where the numbers grow and the knowledge does not.
